title: AngloGerman Manchester
summary: The chapters in this book consider particular Germans living in Manchester from the mid-nineteenth to the late twentieth century, including Frederick Engels, Charles Hallé and other exiles from the 1848 revolutions, W. G. Sebald and refugees from Nazi Germany. The author’s personal family history intersects with these stories. The theme of reparation runs through the book, concluding in a chapter which discusses contemporary Germans working to make amends for the crimes of the Nazi regime.
